title: Exploratory investigation of a non-invasive wearable device for improving bladder management in neurogenic bladder dysfunction
summary: The aim of the planned study is to investigate the extent to which the wearable device inContAlert BladderMate could prevent bladder overdistension. In addition, the impact on quality of life, user-friendliness (for patients and nurses), and the number of incontinence episodes are investigated.
conditions: Bladder paralysis in cases of upper motor neuron lesion
Bladder paralysis in cases of damage to the lower motor neuron
Bladder dysfunction due to spinal shock
Neuromuscular dysfunction of bladder, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name:
One arm with baseline phase and intervention phase thereafter

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Neurogenic bladder dysfunction without sensory bladder feedback 
Adults (18-99) 
Use of intermittent catheterization 
Successful get-to-know phase of the inContAlert BladderMate 
Capacity to consent 
Written consent of the patient to participate in the clinical trial
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy  
Skin disease in the area where the sensor contacts the skin 
Psychiatric disorders 
Inability to consent 
BMI > 40 
In ambulatory setting: Unavailability of a smartphone
